projects.title: Portfolio Website
projects.summary: The website you are looking at: a full-stack portfolio with a React front end and an Express API, built step by step with automated tests, accessibility checks and CI.
projects.description:
A personal portfolio built as a real full-stack application instead of a static page.

The front end is a React single-page app: one long page whose menu scrolls to each section, with its own design system, dark and light themes and an accessible page frame. The server is an Express application that validates its configuration on start and answers with one consistent JSON format.
projects.problem: A portfolio should show engineering ability, not only list it. A static page of links cannot show how its author handles structure, testing, accessibility or security.
projects.solution: Build the portfolio itself as the proof: a monorepo with a React client, an Express server and shared data, checked on every push by automated formatting, linting, tests and a production build.
features: Dark-first design with light and system themes, applied before the first paint so the page never flashes
Keyboard-friendly navigation: a skip link, a menu that works without a mouse, and focus moved to the heading of the section you jump to
Colour contrast of every design token checked against WCAG AA by automated tests
Page content (skills, projects, experience, certificates) lives in files in the repository and is checked by a script, so the site needs no CMS and no login
A contact form checked in the browser and again on the server, with a hidden trap field, a limit per visitor and no personal data in the logs; messages are stored in PostgreSQL
Continuous integration that runs the format check, lint, tests and build on every push

architecture.description: The browser loads a React single-page app that reads its content from files in the repository. The only server feature is the contact form: the Express API validates a message, limits how often one visitor can send, stores it in PostgreSQL and can email a notification.

layers.name: Frontend
layers.detail: React single-page app built with Vite; content comes from files in the repository

layers.name: API
layers.detail: POST /api/contact for the contact form, plus /healthz and /readyz health checks

layers.name: Backend
layers.detail: Express server with validation, rate limiting and central error handling

projects.challenges: Turning a multi-page site into one long page without losing what pages give for free. Old addresses such as /projects/<slug> redirect to the matching section, the menu marks the section on screen, and a jump to a section waits for content that is still loading so it lands in the right place.

projects.title: Beauty & Wellness Information System
projects.summary: A web application for a beauty and wellness clinic, built for a Web Programming course.
projects.description:
A web application for a beauty and wellness clinic (Lipalas Beauty Clinic), built with PHP, MySQL and Bootstrap. Visitors browse the treatments and send appointment requests, and the clinic follows them up in an admin dashboard.

A course project for Web Programming.
features: Treatment list grouped into Face, Body and Consultation, each with a duration, a price and an expandable description
Customers send an appointment request and follow its status, which stays pending until the clinic confirms it
Admin dashboard with booking totals, a status filter and search, and the option to change a booking's status or date, or delete it

projects.title: Travel Jogja Recommendation Web
projects.summary: A decision-support web app that ranks tourist destinations in Yogyakarta with the SAW method, a group project for the SCPK practicum.
projects.description:
A decision-support web application that recommends tourist destinations in Yogyakarta, built with Python and Streamlit. The data of 436 destinations is read from a CSV file and ranked with the Simple Additive Weighting (SAW) method on five criteria: rating, ticket price, distance from the city centre, type of attraction and popularity. Users set the weight of each criterion, filter by type of attraction and maximum ticket price, then explore the calculation steps, the ranking, charts and a map.

Every criterion value is derived from the dataset itself: distance is calculated from the coordinates with the haversine formula, the type score from the average rating per type of attraction, and popularity from grouping the ratings.

A group project for the SCPK practicum.
projects.problem: With hundreds of destinations, choosing is hard when rating, ticket price, distance, type and popularity all matter, and matter differently to each traveller.
projects.solution: Score every destination with Simple Additive Weighting, let the user decide how much each criterion counts, and show every step of the calculation so the ranking can be checked rather than trusted blindly.
features: The weights of the five criteria are set by the user and must add up to 100
Filtering by type of attraction and maximum ticket price
The SAW steps are shown: decision matrix, normalisation and weights
A ranking table with the top three destinations highlighted
An interactive map of the destinations with Folium
